ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, within $\angle AOB$ there are 3 rays $OC$, $OD$, $OE$. If $\angle AOC= 51^\circ$, $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{3}\angle BOC$, $\angle BOD=\frac{1}{3}\angle AOB$, then what is the degree measure of $\angle DOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle BOE = x$,\\
since $\angle BOE= \frac{1}{3}\angle BOC$,\\
thus, $\angle BOC=3\angle BOE=3x$,\\
consequently, $\angle AOB=\angle AOC+\angle BOC=51^\circ+3x$.\\
Since $\angle BOD= \frac{1}{3}\angle AOB$,\\
thus, $\angle BOD= \frac{1}{3}\times(51^\circ+3x)=17^\circ+x$,\\
therefore, $\angle DOE=\angle BOD-\angle BOE=17^\circ+x-x=\boxed{17^\circ}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle BOE = x$. Since $\angle BOE = \frac{1}{3}\angle BOC$, we have $\angle BOC = 3\angle BOE = 3x$. Consequently, $\angle AOB = \angle AOC + \angle BOC = 51^\circ + 3x$. Since $\angle BOD = \frac{1}{3}\angle AOB$, we get $\angle BOD = \frac{1}{3}(51^\circ + 3x) = 17^\circ + x$. Therefore, $\angle DOE = \angle BOD - \angle BOE = 17^\circ + x - x = \boxed{17^\circ}$.
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: From the attached figure, it can be seen that all rays start from point O, forming angle AOB. The rays, in order from top to bottom, are OA, OC, OD, OE, OB. Therefore, ∠BOD is composed of ∠BOE and ∠EOD, that is, ∠BOD = ∠BOE + ∠DOE; at the same time, ∠AOB is composed of ∠AOC and ∠COB, that is, ∠AOB = ∠AOC + ∠BOC. Reasoning: It is known that ∠AOC = 51°, ∠BOE = (1/3)∠BOC, so ∠BOC = 3∠BOE. It is also known that ∠BOD = (1/3)∠AOB, so 3∠BOD = ∠AOB. From the composition relationship of the angles in the figure, ∠BOD = ∠BOE + ∠DOE, ∠AOB = 51° + ∠BOC = 51° + 3∠BOE. Substituting into 3∠BOD = ∠AOB gives 3(∠BOE + ∠DOE) = 51° + 3∠BOE. Expanding and eliminating 3∠BOE gives 3∠DOE = 51°, so ∠DOE = 17°.
